description: This Corvane Medicare Advantage Choice (PPO) statement for March 2026 has three claims. Claim 1 prints the same eye exam twice, with the same date and code, so the member is charged the $40 eye-exam copay two times. Claim 2 (lab tests) and the third claim are processed correctly. A careful reviewer should treat the second eye-exam line as a duplicate and conclude the member owes one copay, not two.

sources.what: An exact duplicate matches another claim line on beneficiary, provider, date of service, procedure code and billed amount
sources.source: CMS, Medicare Claims Processing Manual (Pub. 100-04), ch. 1, §120.2 Exact Duplicates, https://www.cms.gov/regulations-and-guidance/guidance/manuals/downloads/clm104c01.pdf

sources.what: CMS treats payments for the same beneficiary, code and service date by the same provider, beyond the code's daily unit limit, as duplicates
sources.source: CMS Recovery Audit Program, topic 0091 Duplicate Claims - Professional Services, https://www.cms.gov/Research-Statistics-Data-and-Systems/Monitoring-Programs/Medicare-FFS-Compliance-Programs/Recovery-Audit-Program/Approved-RAC-Topics-Items/0091-Exact-Duplicate-Claims

sources.what: Review each statement for accuracy and compare it with your own calendar of appointments, tests and X-rays
sources.source: Medicare.gov, Protecting Yourself From Fraud (CMS Product No. 10111), https://www.medicare.gov/publications/10111-protecting-yourself-from-fraud.pdf
